acv.quote: We proposed six hundred K a year.

header.reason: Angela, the COO, chose Adyen's store rollout team and one vendor for tills and web, while we only described till returns. Tom believed Raj decided and that we were ahead.

findings.label: What started it
findings.finding: Aim store messaging at online orders that stores can't return.
findings.why: The story everyone there tells is Angela watching the returns queue on December 27th.
findings.quote: The store couldn't see the online order

findings.label: Who decided
findings.finding: Get regular time with the COO who owns the stores.
findings.why: Angela signed with Adyen, but Tom treated Raj as the decider and met her only once.

findings.label: The competitor
findings.finding: Bring people who have run store rollouts to store meetings.
findings.why: Raj told Tom that Adyen brought a store rollout team. Later, 11 of 14 questions were about stores.
findings.quote: they came in with a retail team, people who'd done store rollouts

findings.label: Our message
findings.finding: Replace the 'one platform' slide with a step-by-step till return.
findings.why: Bev dismissed our 'unified commerce' slide and asked how a return works at the till.

findings.label: Missing proof
findings.finding: Build a live demo of an online order returned at a till.
findings.why: Angela's team asked to watch a return live at a till, and we only described it.
findings.quote: We described it. We never showed it.

findings.label: Their words
findings.finding: Say 'the tills' and 'one customer, one basket', not 'unified commerce'.
findings.why: Bev and Angela never said 'unified commerce'. We said 'point of sale' while they said 'the tills'.
findings.quote: One system for the tills and the website.
